summary: Isaiah describes a farmer scattering black cumin on level ground and beating out its seeds with a stick. He names ordinary cumin alongside it.

senses.definition: A seed crop traditionally identified as Nigella sativa. Isaiah singles it out as a crop that calls for light threshing.

evidence.note: On the prepared soil the farmer scatters black cumin, then sows cumin and several cereals.
The name occurs twice as Isaiah contrasts the threshing sledge with the stick used to beat out this seed.

evidence.locator: s.v. qṣḥ, plural qṣḥm in KTU 4.751:8, listed by measure with dried figs and raisins

cognates.note: The Arabic has z in the middle. Its range includes cumin and coriander seeds.

evidence.locator: p. 2520, n35580, compared under Ugaritic qṣḥ in DULAT

note: Targum Jonathan on Isa.28.25 and 28.27 uses Aramaic קִצְחָא alongside its word for ordinary cumin. This translation witnesses the traditional distinction. The Ugaritic measurement comes from a separate agricultural inventory. Isaiah gives no description of the plant’s flowers or seed colour.
